title.narrative: SI Refugees: WASH & Livelihood improvements for Eritrean Refugees & host communities in Afar & Amhara regions, Ethiopia

description.narrative: Contribute to the basic needs of refugees and vulnerable communities and their well-being with dignity through improved access to health, food and nutrition security and WASH services.A total of 40,000 people in and around the Dabat and Aysaita refugee camps are using and maintaining safe drinking water sources and sanitation facilities, practising better hygiene and nutrition practices, and engaging in income-generating activities through the active participation of the population.

In the Afar and Amhara regions, where resources are limited, approximately 70,000 Eritrean refugees face significant challenges. The project focuses on improving Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) conditions and livelihood opportunities for both refugees and host communities. It targets food security by enhancing access to nutritious food, while also addressing WASH needs by improving clean water access and sanitation facilities. Additionally, the project aims to boost livelihoods through skill-building and income-generating activities, promoting self-reliance and resilience. This comprehensive approach addresses immediate necessities while striving for sustainable improvements in the well-being of vulnerable populations in the area.

The project aims to directly benefit 40,000 refugees and host community members in water supply, sanitation, and income generation. Selection adheres to UNHCR and RRS guidelines, prioritizing women, local community members, and vulnerable groups such as survivors of SGBV and people with disabilities. Additionally, 50,000 residents of Dabat and Aysaita districts will indirectly benefit from improved services and agricultural products. Community-level organizations and RRS will receive capacity-building support. Facilitators include government organizations at Woreda and Kebele levels, enhancing project impact and sustainability. The total direct beneficiaries amount to 40,000 individuals, calculated based on an average household size of 5 people.
